triage.verifier_justification: The diff does not re-ground or correct any formula: it deletes the section module's entire executable surface (six rules plus a 351-line test file, which becomes `[]`) and replaces it with `status: deferred` plus per-subsection deferred_outputs, and every reason written into the added metadata cites missing dependency surfaces or de-duplication ("the broader gross-income and deduction surface is available", "The chapter-wide deduction inventory is not yet encoded", "without duplicating those executable standard-deduction rules"), never a disagreement with the §63 text. The deleted formulas in fact tracked the resolved corpus text closely — 63(a) gross income minus chapter deductions other than the standard deduction, 63(b)'s seven enumerated subtractions, 63(d)'s exclusion set, 63(e)(1)'s election gate — so "untraceable_branch" (a branch with no basis in the source, removed or re-grounded) does not describe what was removed. Corroborating this as a de-scoping rather than a fidelity fix: the module has never been re-encoded (at HEAD it is still `rules: []` deferred, only path-moved by 86ec136fd), the manifest records tool "axiom-encode deterministic/manual repair", and the squash bullets are validation-driven ("Repair RuleSpec validation coverage"). The remaining substantive edit is the summary being refreshed to match the corpus text verbatim (adding the (c) and (f) text and the "So in original" footnote), which is mechanical provenance.

triage.verifier_notes: Refutation of the first reader: the first reader's two observations about the PRE-fix content are factually correct — the resolved provision (release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, expression_date 2025-12-03, text sha 7fa5f5d7...) contains no zero floor anywhere in §63, so `max(0, ...)` in all four money rules was ungrounded, and stamping `effective_from: '2026-01-01'` on 63(a)/(d)/(e) definitions that long predate 2026 is a period error. But neither is what this change addresses: the fix deletes those rules wholesale together with the grounded parts, so the change cannot be attributed to the clamp or the date, and nothing is re-grounded. If a reviewer insists on keeping this row as a defect, wrong_period_or_effective_date is better supported by the deleted content than untraceable_branch (the deleted branches quote §63 nearly verbatim; the 2026-01-01 stamps have no source basis at all) — but both would be inferred by the reader, not evidenced by the fix. Other facts a reviewer may want: 26/63/a, /b, /d, /e subsection modules do not exist at this commit (only 63/c, 63/c/5, 63/f), so the deferred_outputs point at surfaces that are planned, not present; the pre-fix module computed taxable income from free-floating inputs (`gross_income`, `deductions_allowable_under_this_chapter`, `deductions_allowed_by_this_chapter_other_than_standard_deduction`) that were raw test inputs rather than encoded rules, which is an executability/coverage gap rather than a meaning mismatch. Under the task's own definition this change is not mechanical (outputs and formulas were removed), so "mechanical" is wrong even though the summary/excerpt part of it is.
